lesson_title: One Goat, One Wheel: Circles and Tangents Decoded
hook_text: A goat on a tight rope and a wheelbarrow wheel on concrete — between them they crack every circle-and-tangent question you will ever meet.
clip_script: Clip a goat to a peg with a rope 5 metres long and let it walk with the rope stretched tight. The lap it walks is every point exactly 5 from the peg — a circle, and its equation is just the distance formula: x minus a squared, plus y minus b squared, equals r squared. Reading one takes two questions. What makes each bracket zero? That is the centre — x plus 2 means the peg sits at minus 2. What is the root of the right side? That is the rope — 25 stores a radius of 5. Now the wheel. A wheelbarrow wheel touches smooth concrete at exactly one point, and the spoke to that point hits the concrete at a perfect right angle. Axle, spoke, concrete — centre, radius, tangent — and a right angle means gradients multiplying to minus 1. So any tangent costs four small stops: confirm the point is on the circle, take the spoke's gradient with rise over run, flip it and negate it, and write the line through the point. Substitute the point back, watch it balance, done. One goat, one wheel, every mark.
visual_style: A goat pacing a tight lap around a steel peg, its path snapping onto a crisp coordinate-grid circle, then a wheelbarrow wheel rolling across with one glowing spoke locking perpendicular to the concrete at the contact point.
mood: Calm, earthy, quietly confident — a backyard picture turning into exam-ready machinery.
pacing: One slow lap with the goat, two sharp reading questions, then four brisk beats through the tangent stops.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read any circle equation at a glance.
